static.title: Weigh a cluster by how fast it jitters
static.note: A cluster does not rotate, so there is no curve to plot. What there is instead is a spread of speeds, and the virial theorem turns a spread of speeds into a mass: M = (5/3)·R·⟨v²⟩/G.

presets.label: Coma, done right
presets.note: A spectrograph gives one velocity component out of three, so ⟨v²⟩ = 3σ². This is the measurement Zwicky made, and it needs about ten times more mass than the galaxies and gas can supply.

presets.label: Forget the factor of 3
presets.note: Using σ² alone throws away two of the three directions the galaxies are moving in, and the mass comes out three times too small. This is the commonest mistake in the calculation.

presets.label: Forget to square it
presets.note: Using σ rather than σ² is not an approximation, it is a different quantity with different units. The answer is out by a factor of a thousand and the discrepancy vanishes — which is how you know something went wrong.

static.title: Where the mass of the universe is
static.note: Planck 2018 for the split between dark energy, dark matter and ordinary matter; the stellar share of ordinary matter is the usual census figure. Step through the layers.

presets.label: Everything
presets.note: Dark energy is most of it, and it is not mass at all: it is a property of space that makes the expansion speed up. Set it aside and look at the matter.

presets.label: Just the matter
presets.note: Of the matter, five parts in six are dark. Everything ever seen through a telescope is the remaining sixth.

presets.label: Just the ordinary matter
presets.note: And of that ordinary sixth, most is thin gas between the galaxies. Stars are a small fraction of it.

presets.label: Just the stars
presets.note: Stars are about half a percent of the universe. The rotation curves you measured are one of the ways that was worked out.

static.title: La misma curva, dos explicaciones
static.note: El ajuste con halo y MOND, evaluados con los mismos puntos. Cambia entre ellos y ajusta el disco hasta que cada uno coincida. Fíjate en lo que hubo que decirle a cada uno.

controls.label: Masa del disco (las estrellas que ves)

presets.label: Mejor ajuste con halo
presets.note: La descomposicion que genero esta curva: un disco de 3,3e10 y un halo cuya velocidad plana y radio de nucleo se ajustaron hasta coincidir. Tres numeros ajustados y una coincidencia exacta.

presets.label: Mejor ajuste MOND
presets.note: MOND con el disco que prefiere: 2,1e10, unas dos terceras partes de las estrellas del ajuste con halo, y ningun halo. Un numero ajustado y una coincidencia dentro de las barras de error.

samples.label: Ajuste con halo
samples.value: 2.1 km/s — dentro de las barras de error · 3 numeros ajustados

samples.label: Velocidad plana de MOND para este disco
Que muestra esto
samples.value: Esta explicación reproduce los puntos. La otra también lo hace, con su propia masa de disco y con un número distinto de parámetros ajustados. La curva por sí sola no decide entre ellas.
